newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary Matav starts HUF 4 bln business comms unit.
newsitem.headline: Hungary Matav starts HUF 4 bln business comms unit.

text.p: Hungary's telecommunications company Matav Rt has launched MatavCom, a wholly-owned unit with four billion forints capital, in a move to streamline its loss-making PABX business, officials said on Wednesday.
"We plan to make a profit of some 30 million forints this year," MatavCom General Director Erik Bedo told a news conference.
He added that Matav's PABX (private automatic branch exchange) business made a loss of some 600 to 700 million forints in 1995. He gave no figures for 1996.
Bedo said that most of Matav's four billion investment was contribution in kind and he was not expecting further cash injections from the parent company.
"I would regard the need for future cash injections as a personal failure," he said.
Matav, Hungary's largest telecommunications company, is 67 percent owned by a 50-50 consortium of Ameritech and Deutsche Telekom.
Matav's share of Hungary's PABX market has fallen from 100 percent in 1990 to some 60 percent, Bedo said.
"Our aim is to maintain over 50 percent market share and possibly increase it," he said.
MatavCom, with a workforce of 950, has taken over Matav's 10,000-strong PABX client base and plans to offer complete business solutions as a "one-stop-shopping" provider, Bedo said.
Bedo said MatavCom is in the process of choosing its subcontractors and will select more than one from those currently present on the Hungarian market.
These include the major foreign PABX providers, Siemens, Bosch, AT&T, Alcatel and Ericsson, he said.
